newsitem.title: USA: Florida Progress Q2 hurt by nuclear outage.
newsitem.headline: Florida Progress Q2 hurt by nuclear outage.

text.p: Florida Progress Corp said Tuesday its second quarter loss of $38.2 million, or $0.39 per share, was due to costs associated with the extended outage of the company's Crystal River nuclear power plant.
This compared with earnings of $58.8 million, or $0.61 per share, for the same quarter last year before a $25 million charge to reflect the spin-off of Echelon International Corp.

Florida Power Corp, the company's largest subsidiary, reported a loss of $43.6 million, or $0.45 per share, after costs related to the extended outage of its nuclear plant which began in September 1996. The plant is expected to return to service by the end of 1997.

Florida Progress said second quarter variations reflect $92 million in additional operating and maintenance costs associated with the outage and $70 million for non-recoverable replacement power costs.
Excluding the effect of one-time nuclear outage costs, Florida Power earned $56.1 million, or $0.58 per share, compared with $53.9, or $0.56 per share, a year earlier.
